To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the genetic variants and interactions between genetic and environmental factors modulate individual responses to energy-restricted low-fat and high-protein diets.

different genetic variants and interactions among them with environmental factors (i.e., age, sex, and lifestyle factors) modulate the differential responses of overweight/obese individuals to energy-restricted LF and MHP dietary interventions.
different genetic variants and interactions between these variants and environmental factors modulate individual responses to MIP and LF dietary interventions in overweight/obese individuals.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the identification of the most influential factors that contribute to the differential individual adiposity responses to energy-restricted LF and MHP diets, which are relevant for personalized nutritional strategies in overweight/obese populations.
the study of the influence of genetics on two adiposity phenotypes [waist circumference and total body fat reduction] in response to two hypocaloric diets in subjects with overweight and obesity.
the development of personalized nutrition approaches based on genetic and lifestyle information to optimize the prescription of hypocaloric diets for the management of excessive body weight.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the present results provide evidence that genetic variants, lifestyle factors (physical activity level, energy intake, and macronutrient composition), and their interactions modulate the differential adiposity responses to MHP or LF dietary interventions, thus supporting the use of a personalized nutritional prescription for the prevention and management excessive body weight.

the present study provides evidence of a significant contribution of genetics to individual variability in the response of two adiposity phenotypes (waist circumference reduction [WCR] and total body fat reduction [TFATL]) to two energy-restricted diets with a different macronutrient profile (low-fat [LF] diet and moderately high-protein [MHP] diet).
the genetic information is a useful tool in order to predict the individual responses to different dietary interventions, but it is not a magic tool to prescribe a personalized nutritional strategy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
genetic and lifestyle factors interact to modulate the differential adiposity outcomes in response to energy restricted diets with different macronutrient composition.

genetic variants and interactions between genes and lifestyle factors may help to predict adiposity phenotypes in response to energy restricted diets, and this knowledge could be useful to personalize nutritional strategies for obesity prevention and management.
genetic and environmental factors are important contributors of the variability of the individual response to energy-reduced diets.
The main takeaway from our work is that
personalized nutritional prescriptions for weight control should be tailored not only to genetic but also environmental factors.
the use of genetic information and its interactions with lifestyle/clinical factors may be a powerful tool to improve personalized nutritional strategies for the management of obesity.
personalized nutritional strategies for the treatment of overweight and obesity are feasible, as they are based on a combination of genetic and environmental factors.
